answer: Divergent Challenge Windows: each identity must answer a fresh random cipher challenge within a tight window, and witnesses retain only a hash ledge of prior responses. A clone sharing state can replay identical answers, but cannot produce divergent nonces under time pressure without forking its own memory. Any echo of a prior response from a separate identity triggers flagging. Attacker cost: one full independent compute-and-storage stack per identity, plus forced desynchronization overhead.
